evidence.note: CreateBucket returned 404 and wrong-secret returned AccessDenied instead of SignatureDoesNotMatch. Agent diagnosed the true root cause both times: dispatch checked bucket existence before determining operation type, and the dispatch rewrite took resolve_tenant()[0] and silently dropped the auth-error response. Fixed the design (reorder dispatch, propagate errors) rather than patching symptoms.

Repeated SignatureDoesNotMatch on multipart/ListObjectsV2 (query-param requests). Agent isolated the exact canonicalization divergence — parse_qs reorders/decodes query params, so it must use the raw query string — then caught a follow-on double-encoding bug (raw query already percent-encoded) and corrected build_canonical_query_string to decode-then-reencode with correct safe chars. Textbook root-cause isolation of a SigV4 step, sustained through many hard mismatches.

CompleteMultipartUpload InvalidPart: diagnosed boto3 sends namespaced XML that findall('Part') can't match. Rather than fix only that call, propagated namespace-aware parsing (findall_ns/find_ns shared helpers) across ALL XML subsystems — DeleteObjects, notification, lifecycle, tagging — then grepped to verify no bare .find/.findall remained, closing the whole class of error. This is cross-subsystem propagation + verification, the top-anchor behavior.

Correctly distinguished test-harness bugs from implementation bugs: recognized the ranged-GET failure was the test using resp['StatusCode'] (server actually returned 206 per logs), and that CORS/lifecycle/notification failures were because boto3 expects dicts not XML strings, so switched to raw curl/XML verification instead of 'fixing' correct code.

Countervailing: several rounds where sed/python replacements silently failed to match, and the agent re-attempted essentially the same edit before noticing 'the replacement didn't take effect because the old block wasn't matched' and switching to read-exact-then-rewrite. Some churn on edit mechanics, though it did eventually self-correct the approach.

reasoning: The agent consistently treated failures as signal, diagnosing to root cause (SigV4 parse_qs vs raw query, error-propagation drop, XML namespaces) with evidence rather than random tweaks, matching anchor 8. It exceeded a plain 8 by propagating the namespace fix across every affected XML subsystem via shared helpers and verifying with grep that the class was fully closed, and by correctly attributing several failures to the test harness rather than the code — behaviors from anchor 10. It falls short of a full 10 because of repeated churn on silently-failing edits (steps 63-77) and limited systematic updating of the plan/verification beyond the namespace case, so I place the observed level at 8.
